question: Before initiating a TNF-alpha inhibitor (e.g., etanercept, adalimumab) in a patient with refractory rheumatoid arthritis, which of the following is MANDATORY?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: DEXA is useful for baseline and monitoring of glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis but is not a mandatory pre-biologic requirement. Anti-TNF therapy itself does not require DEXA before initiation.

answers.text: Screening for latent tuberculosis with tuberculin skin test (TST) or IGRA

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. TNF-alpha is essential for granuloma formation and containment of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Anti-TNF therapy can reactivate latent TB — which has high mortality. All patients must be screened with TST or IGRA (plus chest X-ray) before starting any biologic DMARD; latent TB requires prophylactic isoniazid for at least 4 weeks before biologic initiation.
Echocardiography is not a routine mandatory pre-biologic investigation for RA, though cardiac assessment is part of overall RA management (RA carries increased cardiovascular risk).
Colonoscopy has no role in routine pre-biologic screening for RA. It may be relevant before certain biologics used in inflammatory bowel disease but not for anti-TNF therapy in RA.

overallFeedback.feedback: TB screening is the critical pre-biologic mandatory step. TNF-alpha is required to maintain the granuloma that walls off latent Mycobacterium tuberculosis; its inhibition risks fatal reactivation. Always check TST or IGRA + CXR before prescribing any anti-TNF or other biologic DMARD.

Correct. TB screening (TST/IGRA + CXR) is mandatory before ALL biologic DMARDs. TNF-alpha blockade disrupts granuloma integrity, risking TB reactivation. Latent TB must be treated with isoniazid (minimum 4 weeks before biologic start).
